papers.title: The Zero-Age Massive Stellar Population of W49A from VLA Observations
papers.abstract: We use all-configuration VLA data at 3.3 cm with a physical resolution of ~2000 AU to infer the embedded zero-age massive stellar population of the W49A protocluster, as traced by its compact, ultracompact (UC), and hypercompact (HC) H II regions. Our method consists of visual source identification, the derivation of stellar ionizing-photon rates from the observed emission measure, and the further derivation of stellar masses and luminosities using state-of-the-art stellar calibrations. Considering the 101 robust detections, maximum-likelihood estimation fitting of the high-mass end (M > 10.9 M_\odot) of the sample yields power-law slopes Gamma >= 2.40 for the logarithmic representation of the stellar initial mass function (IMF): dN/d(log M) proportional to M^{-Gamma}. The result is robust considering different assumptions for the ionizing stellar systems. The slopes remain at Gamma >= 1.88 after correction for optical depth effects at 3.3 cm. Therefore, the inferred distribution of stellar masses presents a clear deficit in the high-mass end as compared to the standard stellar IMF (Gamma = 1.35). We propose that this is due to a shorter lifetime of the radio-detected H II regions produced by higher-mass stars, but evolutionary effects in the mass distribution of star formation within embedded protoclusters cannot be discarded.
papers.comments: Resubmitted to the AAS Journals after addressing the third referee report

papers.title: Gravitational Waves from Green's Function Decomposition for a Kerr black hole: I. Equatorial ISCO Plunge
papers.abstract: We present a decomposition of the Kerr Green's function in the time domain, motivated by the frequency-domain split previously studied in the Schwarzschild limit. We show that the identification of a quasinormal-mode contribution, a direct part, and a late-time tail is still available, where the split times are determined by the black hole spin and positions of the emitter and receiver. We have checked this Green's function with time-domain Teukolsky numerical simulations and find excellent agreement. We also apply this decomposed Green's function in the time domain to a model problem with a test particle plunging into a Kerr black hole. The dynamically excited direct wave and quasinormal modes are obtained by convoluting the Green's function with the particle's source term, which may be viewed as the first order in mass ratio of a spinning black hole ringdown.

papers.title: A Buchdahl solution generator for Einstein-sigma gravity and multiscalar-tensor gravity
papers.abstract: Buchdahl transformations provide a geometric route from vacuum spacetimes to scalar-field solutions. We formulate this mechanism as a target-covariant solution generator for Einstein gravity coupled to nonlinear sigma models in $D>3$ dimensions. On any connected region in which a Ricci-flat seed admits a non-null hypersurface-orthogonal cyclic coordinate with fixed-sign nonzero norm, the logarithm of that norm defines a Buchdahl potential $\Sigma$. A one-parameter redistribution of the cyclic norm then generates the exact Ricci source $R_{AB}=C_D(\beta)\partial_A\Sigma\partial_B\Sigma$, with $C_D(\beta)=\frac{D-2}{D-3}(1-\beta^2)$, while $\Sigma$ remains harmonic in the deformed metric. Composing $\Sigma$ with an affinely parametrized geodesic of a non-degenerate target metric whose squared speed is $C_D(\beta)$ therefore yields an exact Einstein--sigma-model solution. For positive-definite targets, the corresponding pullback condition also implies that the nontrivial scalar map has one-dimensional image; for indefinite targets, the geodesic ansatz remains a sufficient solution-generating sector but need not exhaust all possible realizations of the same rank-one spacetime source. Through the Einstein/Jordan-frame correspondence, the construction gives vacuum tensor-multiscalar solutions as well. We illustrate the unified generator with flat, spherical, hyperbolic and axion-dilaton targets and with Tangherlini, Weyl, Kasner, Rosen-wave, Gowdy, Kaluza-Klein bubble and C-metric seeds. The result separates cleanly the geometric Buchdahl source from its target-space realization and extends this rank-one cyclic sector across static, cosmological, wave and accelerating geometries.

papers.title: Black hole apparent horizons become comoving with the universe
papers.abstract: It has been shown that static black hole event horizons cannot exist in time-dependent backgrounds without becoming naked singularities. In light of this, we are left with the question ''how does a black hole horizon evolve in an expanding universe?'' Here we offer a solution to this puzzle by showing that spherically symmetric black hole apparent horizons tend to become comoving, thus confirming the necessity of a cosmological coupling and raising intriguing possibilities for the early growth of black holes.
papers.comments: Version accepted by Physical Review Letters

papers.title: Stationary Rotating Geometries Associated with Nonsingular Pulsating Collapse
papers.abstract: Since the first exact solutions of General Relativity (GR) were obtained, it became clear that the theory predicts a new class of compact objects: black holes. The Hawking--Penrose singularity theorems show that, under appropriate assumptions, gravitational collapse in GR leads to singular behavior. Motivated by the expectation that such regimes require physics beyond classical GR, effective approaches inspired by Loop Quantum Cosmology (LQC) and braneworld scenarios introduce high-density corrections. In this work we consider the static exterior geometry introduced by Gao, Lu, Shen, and Faraoni, associated with a comoving interior model in which the singularity is avoided through a sequence of collapse and bounce phases. Using the Newman--Janis algorithm in the Azreg-Aïnou formulation, we construct a stationary rotating exterior extension of this geometry. The resulting line element describes a stationary axisymmetric rotating spacetime whose horizon geometry, angular velocity, surface gravity, and Hawking temperature recover the Kerr and Schwarzschild limits when the quantum/braneworld correction becomes negligible ($l\to 0$). We further analyze the thermal response at fixed rotational state-space parameter, identify Davies-type singular points, and formulate an extended thermodynamic state-space relation.
papers.comments: Version published in General Relativity and Gravitation. 22 pages, 4 figures

papers.title: Late-time dark energy dynamics in $f(Q)$ gravity: A data-driven analysis
papers.abstract: The increasing precision and complementarity of late-time cosmological observations provide new opportunities to test modified gravity against the observed expansion history of the universe. The combination of DESI DR2 BAO measurements with cosmic chronometers (CC) and independent Type Ia supernova compilations provides a data-driven test of cosmic acceleration. Motivated by this progress, we investigate late-time dark energy dynamics in symmetric teleparallel $f(Q)$ gravity by adopting the power-law form $f(Q)=\beta Q^{m+1}$ and characterizing cosmic evolution through the effective equation of state (EoS) parameter. The model is constrained using CC, DESI DR2 BAO and three independent Type Ia supernova compilations, namely Pantheon+, DES-Dovekie and Union3. The inferred Hubble constant values are mutually consistent, yielding $H_0=68.0^{+2.7}_{-3.3}$, $68.2^{+2.7}_{-3.3}$ and $67.4^{+2.7}_{-3.3}\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, respectively. Statistically, the proposed $f(Q)$ model yields lower $\chi^2_{\min}$ values and is favored by the AIC for all dataset combinations, whereas the BIC favors $\Lambda$CDM for the CC + DESI DR2 + Pantheon+ and CC + DESI DR2 + DES-Dovekie combinations and indicates no meaningful preference between the two models for the CC + DESI DR2 + Union3 dataset combinations. The reconstructed effective EoS characterizes the evolution of the cosmic fluid, while the deceleration parameter indicates the current accelerated expansion of the universe. Higher-order cosmographic parameters and the Statefinder and $Om(z)$ diagnostics provide complementary insights into the evolution of the cosmic expansion, while the Statefinder trajectories approach the $\Lambda$CDM fixed point in the far future. Overall, the power-law $f(Q)$ model provides a competitive description of the late-time expansion history and the observed cosmic acceleration.
papers.comments: 32 pages, 14 figures, 4 tables, Published in the Journal of High Energy Astrophysics

papers.title: The Einstein Tensor from UV-regulated Field Correlations
papers.abstract: It is known that the spacetime metric can be recovered from quantum field correlators. We extend this programme by showing that the Einstein tensor can be directly written in terms of UV-regulated field correlations. The same correlation structure also directly determines the Ricci tensor, while higher coincidence derivatives recover the connection and Riemann tensor. We further show that the renormalized stress-energy tensor can be formulated within this framework, up to the standard finite renormalization freedom. These results provide a correlation-based organization of the semiclassical Einstein equations and advance the programme of formulating spacetime geometry in terms of quantum field correlations.

papers.title: Fractional Bose-Einstein Condensate Dark Matter Cores: Numerical GPP Solutions and SPARC Rotation Curves
papers.abstract: We investigate a fractional Bose Einstein condensate dark matter scenario in which an ultralight bosonic component forms a self gravitating core embedded in a predominantly cold dark matter halo. The stationary GPP system solved numerically beyond the TF approximation leads to energetically bound equilibrium configurations and good phenomenological fits to the selected rotation curves from 30 SPARC galaxies.

papers.title: Charged Klein--Gordon modes on an Ellis wormhole: magnetic confinement and conditional Heun-polynomial solvability
papers.abstract: We study a charged Klein--Gordon field on the complete $(2+1)$-dimensional Ellis wormhole, coupled to the pullback of a uniform ambient magnetic field. The induced gauge potential is regular, whereas the intrinsic magnetic pseudoscalar reverses sign across the throat. For $\alpha_B>0$, the radial operator is unitarily equivalent to a self-adjoint one-dimensional Schrödinger operator with a smooth confining potential and discrete spectrum. The radial equation is reduced to confluent-Heun form, and polynomial solvability is shown to require two independent termination conditions. These conditions yield degree-zero Gaussian modes, degree-one states of both global parities, and representative degree-two even states. Exact Ellis-measure normalization is obtained for the degree-zero and degree-one modes. An independent fourth-order full-line finite-difference calculation validates the analytic benchmarks and determines the first eight eigenvalues and their parities. In the double-well regime, the forbidden-region action determines the leading semiclassical exponential of the even--odd level splitting.

papers.title: Unified spatiotemporal quantum states and spatiotemporal entanglement from Kirkwood-Dirac phase space
papers.abstract: The notion of a spatiotemporal quantum state extends the conventional concept of a spatial quantum state to the spatiotemporal domain. Such states are represented by unit-trace operators that encode correlations among quantum events distributed across space and time. In this work, we use the spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac phase space to provide a unified characterization of spatiotemporal quantum states. Spatiotemporal states obtained from Kirkwood-Dirac distributions are generally non-Hermitian and nonnormal; whereas those constructed from Margenau-Hill distributions are Hermitian. We provide a unification via (quasi)probabilistic mixture of Kirkwwod-Dirac spatiotemporal states which encompasses almost all existing formulations of spatiotemporal quantum states. We derive recursive expressions for spatiotemporal states and elucidate the relation between Kirkwood-Dirac nonclassicality and the temporality of spatiotemporal states. We further extend the construction to many-fold correlation functions and establish its connection with out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs). We also develop a more general unifying framework based on (quasi)probabilistic mixture of $s$-parametrized spatiotemporal states and establish their Petz time reversal and application in studying Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) condition in two-time setting. Finally, we apply this framework to characterize quantum entanglement in spacetime and analyze spatiotemporal entanglement using several complementary entropy measures.

papers.title: Black Holes and Scalar Propagation in Three-Dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet Gravity
papers.abstract: We derive an analytic black-hole family in three-dimensional scalar--tensor Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity with positive coupling. A single implicit equation determines the static circular metric and a scalar linear in time. We show that these solutions exhaust regular nonextremal exteriors with the stated AdS boundary conditions and a fixed nonzero coefficient of time in the scalar. The coupled metric and scalar perturbations have one propagating degree of freedom. On one branch, its kinetic coefficient is positive, its equation is hyperbolic throughout the exterior, and its bulk spatial energy is positive for perturbations of compact support. Scalar signals can cross the metric horizon outward, so exterior evolution needs information from the interior. For linear perturbations with the original metric and scalar boundary values fixed, nonzero compact initial master displacements with zero velocity can evolve only until their first contact with the AdS boundary. We derive this restriction from the original metric and scalar equations.

papers.title: Optical and Dynamical Signatures of Padé Approximated Wormholes in $f(T)$ Gravity
papers.abstract: We construct traversable wormhole solutions in the linear teleparallel model $f(T) = \alpha T + \beta$, adopting Padé approximants of order [1/0] and [0/1] as shape functions together with the redshift function $\Phi(r) = -M/r$, and derive the corresponding source terms from the modified field equations. We assess the physical viability of both configurations through the energy conditions, Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equilibrium, the volume integral quantifier, thin-shell junction matching to an exterior Schwarzschild geometry, embedding diagrams, proper radial distance, the gravitational energy and the active mass. We then examine the observational signatures of each geometry by analysing equatorial null geodesics and the photon-sphere structure, computing shadow maps and radial intensity profiles, ray-tracing relativistic images of a geometrically thin accretion disc, and integrating timelike rosette orbits. Finally, we study the dynamical stability of both wormholes through a third-order WKB quasinormal-mode analysis across scalar, electromagnetic, and axial gravitational perturbations, cross-checked against time-domain evolution and the eikonal photon-sphere correspondence, and examine the parameter dependence of the mode spectrum together with the possibility of trapped-mode echoes.

papers.title: X-ray measurements of the elemental abundances for the diffuse emission in the nuclear starburst galaxy NGC 3079
papers.abstract: Outflows driven by feedback leave imprints on a galaxy's diffuse X-ray emission. Elemental abundances provide key diagnostics of feedback-driven chemical enrichment. We present a spectroscopic study of the diffuse X-ray emission in NGC 3079 using XMM-Newton RGS and EPIC, focusing on the nuclear region and the extended galactic-scale superbubble (GSB). We analyzed the high-resolution RGS spectrum of the central $\sim4\,\mathrm{kpc}$ region, encompassing the $\sim1\,\mathrm{kpc}$ nuclear superbubble (NSB), and the EPIC spectrum of the GSB out to $5'$ ($\sim25\,\mathrm{kpc}$). The nuclear spectrum is best described by a multi-temperature thermal-plasma model plus a charge-exchange (CX) component, which contributes approximately $13\%$ of the total observed energy flux in the 0.2-2 keV band. The best-fit O/Fe and Ne/Fe ratios are $0.47$ and $0.77$ in solar units. Comparing these ratios with initial-mass-function-weighted core-collapse supernova (SNcc) yields gives an upper progenitor-mass cutoff of $M_{\rm u}\simeq13$-$15\,M_\odot$ for pure SNcc enrichment. For the best-fit spectral model, including a Type Ia supernova (SNIa) contribution increases the inferred cutoff, but its $1\sigma$ upper limit remains below $25\,M_\odot$ for SNIa fractions up to $10\%$ within the adopted yield models. The characteristic ages of the NSB and GSB are $0.92^{+0.39}_{-0.46}\,\mathrm{Myr}$ and $29.6^{+1.6}_{-2.9}\,\mathrm{Myr}$, respectively, suggesting episodic feedback in NGC 3079.

papers.title: Conserved currents associated with conformal symmetry in linearized gravity
papers.abstract: Extending a previous work on the energy-momentum tensor of the linearized gravitational field in Minkowski background, conserved currents in linearized gravity associated with Lorentz transformations, dilatations and special conformal transformations are explored in the framework of Lagrangian field theory. Both outstanding special cases and general parametric families of currents are considered. Regarding the former, the distinguished energy-momentum tensor $T_{\mathrm{lg}}^{ab}$ we found earlier, guided by similarities between linearized gravity and electrodynamics, is supplemented with an angular momentum tensor $M_{\mathrm{lg}}^{abc}$ and a dilatation current $D_{\mathrm{lg}}^a$, associated with Lorentz and dilatation symmetries. Concerning special conformal transformations, a generalization of Noether's theorem that is useful if additional conditions (such as gauge fixing conditions) are imposed is formulated, it is shown that special conformal transformations are Noether symmetries of linearized gravity in the generalized harmonic gauges, and a special conformal tensor $C_{\mathrm{lg}}^{ab}$, accompanying $T_{\mathrm{lg}}^{ab}$, is obtained using the generalized Noether's theorem. The angular momentum tensor, dilatation current and special conformal tensor accompanying two other notable energy-momentum tensors are discussed as well. General multi-parameter families of $M^{abc}$, $D^a$ and $C^{ab}$ tensors accompanying a general family of energy-momentum tensors, which was found earlier and includes canonical energy-momentum tensors, are also determined, and local balance equations that are relevant if matter is present are derived for them. Their members do not depend on higher than first derivatives of the linearized metric.
papers.comments: 63 pages, minor corrections, 2 references added, results unchanged

papers.title: MADGRAV: a multilevel anomaly-detection pipeline for gravitational-wave searches applied to LIGO data
papers.abstract: We present the results of \textbf{MADGRAV}, a deep-learning-based search for high-mass compact binary coalescences, applied to the data collected by the LIGO interferometers during the third observing run and during the first and second part of the fourth observing run. The \textbf{MADGRAV} pipeline consists of a series of sequential convolutional neural networks that perform anomaly detection, glitch classification, coherence testing, and signal ranking. Data from the Hanford and Livingston LIGO detectors are studied (both individually and in coherence) by way of 1 second Q-transform windows. Of the candidates that survive every stage of the pipeline, 48 reach the significance threshold, and we report 47 gravitational wave detections characterised by a false alarm rate below $1\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ with a probability of astrophysical origin $p_{\rm astro}>0.9$. Of the 47 detections, 44 are shared with the minimally modelled coherent WaveBurst search. The observed total source-frame masses, extracted from official gravitational wave transient catalogues, are in the $14-236 M_{\odot}$ range with a median of $69 M_{\odot}$, and a median SNR of 16. We note that the recovered fraction of confident detections rises with mass: for LIGO detectors network SNR $>10$ the pipeline recovers $8.1\%$ of confident catalog events below $30 M_{\odot}$, $39.8\%$ between $30$ and $100 M_{\odot}$, and $53.3\%$ above $100 M_{\odot}$, corresponding to $33.3\%$, $45.5\%$ and $53.3\%$ of the events detected by coherent WaveBurst in the same bins. These results suggest that anomaly detection pipelines can serve as an independent detection channel complementary to matched filtering in the high-mass high-SNR regime.

papers.title: From Critical Zero Modes to Interior Dynamics in Holographic Superconductors
papers.abstract: We study how the critical behavior of holographic superconductors controls the interior geometry of charged black holes. Although the exterior condensate vanishes at criticality, the critical zero mode develops logarithmic oscillations near the Reissner--Nordström Cauchy horizon, rendering the interior critical limit nonuniform. We show that the transmitted critical-mode amplitude, together with local Cauchy-horizon quantities, fixes both the leading Einstein--Rosen collapse $\Delta z_{\rm ER}$ width and the phase $\Theta_J$ in the subsequent Josephson regime. If the condensate obeys $t\equiv1-T/T_c\propto\epsilon^{2r}$, then $\Delta z_{\rm ER}\propto t^{1/r}$ and $\Theta_J\propto t^{-1/r}$. This Josephson phase is transferred to the first Kasner epoch, producing oscillatory Kasner exponents and an accumulation law $t_n\sim n^{-r}$ for successive zeros of the scalar velocity. The critical zero mode fixes the leading collapse and phase coefficients, which are quantitatively confirmed by fully nonlinear solutions in both the ordinary and tricritical cases. At low temperature, the interior instead depends on the infrared completion of the zero-temperature geometry. Thus near-critical scaling is governed by critical-mode transmission, whereas the low-temperature behavior is controlled by the infrared endpoint.

papers.title: Analytic parity-violating greybody factors of a dynamical Chern-Simons black hole
papers.abstract: We study the low-frequency scattering of gravitational and pseudoscalar waves off a non-rotating black hole in dynamical Chern-Simons (dCS) gravity, where the axial (odd-parity) gravitational sector is irreducibly coupled to the dynamical pseudoscalar while the polar sector remains general relativistic. Working to first order in the dimensionless coupling zeta = (l_CS/M)^4 and using matched asymptotic expansions, we obtain, for the quadrupole (l=2) channel, an exact closed form for the graviton-to-pseudoscalar conversion probability and a high-precision analytic reconstruction of the absorption (greybody) asymmetry. Both reduce to combinations of pi^4, pi^2, and rational numbers, with no ln2 or odd-zeta terms in the reconstructed basis; the transmission-phase sector, by contrast, is governed by an analytically derived static integral involving Apery's constant zeta(3), with its matching prefactor identified numerically. The parity-violating reflection-phase asymmetry is strongly suppressed at low frequency -- well below the parity-even general-relativistic reflection phase -- so that any polarization rotation imprinted on the reflected wave is negligible, while a subleading O(omega*zeta) asymmetry remains in the transmitted phase. These effects are intrinsically strong-field and low-frequency: the normalized flux asymmetries are consistent with a 1/(M*omega)^2 falloff in the geometric-optics limit, where the leading remaining flux effect is conversion loss. The matched-asymptotic results are checked against direct two-channel integration, and the integral determining the absorption asymmetry is evaluated to high precision within an analytically controlled transcendental basis. The coefficients provide analytic targets linking dCS parity violation in absorption and mode conversion to the axial/polar quasinormal-mode splitting.
papers.comments: 20 pages. v2: revised in response to referee reports -- added the complete two-channel S-matrix at l=2 (new appendix), corrected the reflection-phase discussion (Chandrasekhar-Detweiler relation), and added Love-number, EFT-matching, and QNM connections. Central results d2, kappa2 unchanged. Matches version under review at GRG

papers.title: Discovery of the Slowest Radio Pulsar in the Small Magellanic Cloud
papers.abstract: We report the discovery of a new radio pulsar PSR J0103$-$72 in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) through a reanalysis of Parkes/Murriyang archival observations targeting supernova remnants and pulsar-wind nebulae in the SMC. Previously two pulsars were discovered in these observations, and PSR J0103$-$72 is the third which we independently detected in two observations of its target field. It has a spin period of 1.327 sec and a dispersion measure (DM) of $272\pm13~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$, making it the slowest known radio pulsar in the SMC with the second-highest DM. We did not identify any plausible supernova remnant or pulsar-wind nebula associated with the pulsar. Subtracting the predicted Galactic foreground leaves a DM contribution of $\sim 230$--$242~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$, which may suggest a long path through the ionized medium of the SMC, enhanced ionized gas along the sightline, or both. Although these data had previously been searched using both FFT and fast folding algorithms, our FFT-based reprocessing found PSR J0103$-$72 through search techniques which have previously been highly effective in discovering a large number of pulsars in other surveys. This discovery shows that candidates with weak Fourier-domain significance can reveal faint, narrow-duty cycle pulsars missed in earlier extragalactic pulsar searches.
papers.comments: Accepted for publication in ApJ Letters

papers.title: The XMM Cluster Survey: Cross-Calibration of eROSITA and XMM using Dark Energy Survey Y3 Galaxy Clusters
papers.abstract: We present the cross-calibration of the eROSITA and XMM telescopes, using galaxy clusters detected by redMaPPer from the first three years of Dark Energy Survey observations (DESY3RM). We use the X-ray: Generate and Analyse (XGA) Python module to measure eROSITA properties, and validate our methodology using a deep pointed eROSITA CAL-PV observation of A3158, and a sample of 119 clusters from the expanded HIgh FLux Galaxy Cluster Sample (eeHiFLUGCS). Next, we construct a sample of DESY3RM clusters matched to XMM observations analysed by the XMM Cluster Survey (XCS), and to clusters in the first release of the eROSITA All-Sky Survey (eRASS1). This produced a sample of 114 DESY3RM clusters with both XMM and eROSITA detections. Our resulting X-ray temperatures determined from eROSITA were compared to eRASS1 catalogue values, showing consistency between the two analyses. Comparisons between XMM and eROSITA temperatures reveal a systematic offset, with XMM temperatures 28$\pm$7% higher on average. Finally, we fit $L_{\rm X,soft}$-$\lambda_{\rm RM}$ and $T_{\rm X}$-$\lambda_{\rm RM}$ scaling relations for both eROSITA and XMM using the same cluster sample, finding minimal differences in the $L_{\rm X,soft}$-$\lambda_{\rm RM}$ relation but a clear normalisation offset in the $T_{\rm X}$-$\lambda_{\rm RM}$ relation, particularly for the highest richness systems. This study will enable future work combining eROSITA and XMM observatories for DESY3RM clusters.

papers.title: Adiabatic particle production in a time-dependent accelerated frame
papers.abstract: We study a massive scalar field in flat spacetime written in a time-dependent accelerated frame whose fixed-coordinate observers have maximal proper acceleration at $t=0$ and become asymptotically inertial without forming a horizon. The Klein-Gordon equation separates into a modified Mathieu equation in time and a confining Schrödinger problem in space with a discrete spectrum. We impose an adiabatic vacuum at the instant of maximal acceleration and compute the particle number in the inertial future. For the zeroth-order adiabatic state it falls as the inverse eighth power of the initial mode frequency, and raising the adiabatic order cancels successive terms of the endpoint expansion, in analogy with the switching transients of finite-time detectors. Analytic continuation of the spatial eigenfunctions gives the out modes in closed form and an exact expression for the particle number, which is entirely the mismatch at $t=0$ between the initial state and the out vacuum. The spectrum is algebraic rather than Planckian.

papers.title: Tracing Accretion and Inner-Disk Gas Evolution in the Orion Nebula via Br-alpha and CO
papers.abstract: We present a systematic spectroscopic study of hydrogen Brackett-alpha (Br-alpha) and carbon monoxide (CO) fundamental-band (4.3-5.2 micron) emission from a homogeneous sample of 0.2-1.5 Msun pre-main-sequence (PMS) stars in the Orion Nebula observed with JWST/NIRSpec-MOS as part of our Chandra-JWST project. Using 73 Br-alpha and 46 CO spectra, we investigate correlations between warm-gas emission, stellar properties, accretion, and environment with censored correlation and regression analyses accounting for multiple testing. Br-alpha luminosity correlates strongly with accretion luminosity (Lacc), even after excluding sources within 2' of Theta1 Ori C, the nebula's main ionizing O-type star, whose radiation may bias proplyd Lacc estimates. This supports Br-alpha as a robust empirical tracer of accretion in PMS stars. Br-alpha also correlates with visual extinction (Av) and more weakly with stellar bolometric luminosity and mass. CO fundamental-band luminosities likewise correlate positively with Lacc and Av, relationships that persist in a larger combined JWST/NIRSpec+MIRI sample spanning multiple star-forming regions. In contrast to Br-alpha, CO luminosity shows no significant dependence on basic stellar properties, suggesting that warm molecular gas is governed primarily by accretion and local disk conditions. The weaker correlations of the Spitzer/IRAC spectral slope with Lacc and Av suggest that warm inner-disk gas may evolve or disperse faster than optically thick dust. Overall, the CO results tentatively indicate declining warm-gas emission as disks evolve, modulated by accretion-powered thermal and ultraviolet excitation, although variations in emitting area inherited from natal core conditions may also contribute.
papers.comments: 23 pages, 8 figures, and 2 tables. Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal on November 16, 2026

papers.title: Towards ultrarelativistic scattering near the light ring: asymptotic divergence of gravitational-wave fluxes
papers.abstract: Near the threshold between scattering and capture by a Schwarzschild black hole, a particle spends a long time close to an unstable circular orbit, which in the ultrarelativistic limit approaches the light ring. Here we study the behavior of the gravitational wave fluxes emitted by such an ultrarelativistic particle at first order in the mass ratio. The fluxes radiated to infinity and absorbed by the horizon diverge as the inverse distance from the light ring multiplied by its logarithm. Using the Wentzel, Kramers, and Brillouin (WKB) approximation to solve the Regge-Wheeler equation and treating the infinite harmonic sum analytically, we derive an exact expression for the coefficient of this logarithmic enhancement and show that it is identical for both fluxes. We then estimate the coefficients of the subleading pole contributions by combining numerical calculations at low multipoles with the exact asymptotics at large multipoles. We further conjecture an extension to equatorial circular orbits in Kerr. Interestingly, our results also inform the analytical structure of the energy and angular momentum losses of ultrarelativistic scattering orbits near the light ring. More broadly, our work illustrates how WKB methods can provide the asymptotic behavior of self-force observables in regimes where numerical mode sums become increasingly challenging.
papers.comments: 20 pages + appendices, 9 figures, 2 ancillary data files. v2: improved numerical checks for Kerr

papers.title: High-cadence GW astrometry in the $μ$Hz gap
papers.abstract: We forecast the sensitivity of a dedicated, fast-spinning astrometric survey to a stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) in the microhertz gap between pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) and LISA. Spinning the satellite faster samples each star more often, raising the Nyquist frequency and opening higher frequencies at no cost in noise: the shorter, noisier exposures are exactly compensated by their number, so the white-noise floor of each position stream is independent of cadence. High frequencies are where astrometry is most competitive, because the deflection measures the strain directly: its strain noise is white, whereas the equivalent noise of pulsar timing grows as $f^2$. With a cross-correlation estimator over $N$ reference stars and the astrometric overlap computed in the distant-source limit, we find that a Gaia-like satellite scanning the ecliptic poles, with $N\sim10^4$ bright stars over $10$~yr, falls short of the background measured by PTAs by a factor $\sim\!60$. A larger, $8$-m-class aperture, or a constellation of satellites covering the whole sky, reaches it, while extending the reach continuously across the $\mu$Hz band.

papers.title: Does the Escape Fraction Prescription Shape Reionization History and Morphology?
papers.abstract: The escape fraction of ionizing photons, $f_{\rm esc}$, is among the least constrained quantities of the Epoch of Reionization (EoR), and intergalactic opacity prevents its direct measurement at high redshifts. We constrain three power-law parameterizations, $f_{\rm esc}(z)$, $f_{\rm esc}(M_{\rm h})$, and $f_{\rm esc}(z, M_{\rm h})$, against JWST UV luminosity functions and EoR observables (ionizing emissivity, neutral hydrogen fraction, and Thomson optical depth) using Markov Chain Monte Carlo, with priors allowing $f_{\rm esc}$ to increase or decrease with redshift and halo mass. We propagate the best-fit models into the semi-numerical simulation SimFast21 and compare their ionization morphology and 21 cm power spectra with a constant-$f_{\rm esc}$ model. All models reproduce the observations with nearly identical global reionization histories. The data favor $f_{\rm esc}$ decreasing with redshift, from $\approx 0.8$ at $z = 5$ to $\approx 0.35$ at $z = 15$. The halo-mass-only model prefers $f_{\rm esc}$ increasing with halo mass, but this trend is a proxy for redshift evolution. When both dependencies vary jointly, the data prefer a mass-independent $f_{\rm esc}$. At matched global neutral fraction, all four prescriptions yield similar ionization morphology, and the 21 cm power spectra agree to within $\approx 10\%$. Thus, once calibrated against the same observations, the details of the $f_{\rm esc}$ prescription, set by interstellar medium physics, largely average out in both global observables and the 21 cm power spectrum. Distinguishing them may require statistics beyond the power spectrum, such as Ly$\alpha$ and 21 cm forest sightline statistics, or forecasts that exploit their small differences in reionization timing.

papers.title: Kerr metric perturbations in Lorenz gauge via numerical relativity methods
papers.abstract: Gravitational self-force calculations are needed to accurately describe the motion of a small body in a spinning (Kerr) black hole spacetime, which is vital to predict gravitational wave signals from asymmetric-mass compact binaries. Accurate calculations for the upcoming LISA mission require a minimum of second perturbative order in the mass ratio, which has thus far only been achieved for nonspinning (Schwarzschild) black holes due to nonlinear complexities of the Einstein equations. In this work, we calculate Kerr metric perturbations with a new computational approach based on numerical relativity methods, extending recent scalar self-force results to full general relativity. We formulate the perturbative Lorenz-gauge Einstein equations in terms of azimuthal $m$-modes in the frequency domain and solve the resulting elliptic partial differential equations using a spectral discontinuous Galerkin discretization, adaptive mesh refinement, and preconditioned iterative solvers. With our new method, we achieve exponentially convergent first-order gravitational self-force calculations for circular equatorial orbits in Kerr spacetime up to spin $|a|/M=0.998$ (the Thorne limit). Our framework is designed to carry over to second order by delivering accurate and well-behaved first-order data for nonlinear source construction, and as a solver for the second-order metric perturbations themselves.

papers.title: Direct product geometries in $n$-dimensional linear and quadratic gravity
papers.abstract: Direct-product spacetimes offer a tractable route to exact solutions in gravity theories beyond general relativity. We study $n$-dimensional direct-product spacetimes of $(m_1+m_2)$, $(2+m)$, and $(2+\ldots+2)$ type in linear gravity and general pure quadratic-curvature gravity, allowing the two-dimensional subspaces to have nonconstant curvature. We classify the resulting solution spaces and determine how the allowed geometries depend on the gravitational theory, the dimension, and the curvature couplings. Metrics containing two-dimensional part(s) of nonconstant curvature are governed either by algebraic conditions on a curvature profile, or, in one special class of quadratic gravity, by a differential equation. Relations governing metrics with only constant-curvature $m$ dimensional subspaces are purely algebraic. We compare the two considered theories and study relations between their solution sets. We further examine conformal relations, generalized Petrov types, and compatibility with electromagnetic sources. Four- and six-dimensional cases are analyzed in detail, and so is the Weyl squared action (that reduces to Weyl conformal gravity in $n=4$), as a particular example of quadratic gravity couplings. Explicit analytic solutions illustrating the resulting structure are presented whenever possible.

papers.title: Thermodynamics of Kerr-Newman-Bertotti-Robinson black holes from background subtraction
papers.abstract: The non-asymptotic flatness of the charged rotating black holes immersed in the Bertotti-Robinson magnetic field causes the ambiguity in the gauge choice for the time generator and the electric potential. By using the newly established form of the integrability condition together with the gauge choice for the asymptotically flat charged rotating black holes as the initial condition, we have found that the gauge can be uniquely fixed. With this fixed gauge, we further obtain the mass and angular momentum by the background subtraction method with the Minkowski spacetime as the reference spacetime. As a result, not only is the first law of black hole thermodynamics as well as the quantum statistical relation automatically satisfied, but also both the Christodoulou-Ruffini relation and the Smarr formula are obeyed.
papers.comments: typos corrected, references added, presentation refined

papers.title: The Cool Circumgalactic Echo of the Stellar-to-Halo Mass Relation
papers.abstract: The stellar-to-halo mass relation (SHMR), a key prediction of galaxy formation models, peaks at $M_* \sim 3 \times 10^{10}\,M_\odot$. This scale is often attributed to circumgalactic baryonic feedback processes, however, direct observational evidence linking the two remains scarce. Using Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) galaxy--quasar pairs, we map the cool circumgalactic medium (CGM) using Mg II $\lambda\lambda2796, 2803$ absorption with stacking technique across nearly three decades in stellar mass. The radial Mg II absorption equivalent-width profile, $W_{\rm MgII} \propto D^k$, becomes progressively shallower with increasing stellar mass, following $k = 0.70\log(M_*/M_\odot)-9.12$. Crucially, we find that the $W_{\rm MgII}$ in the CGM scales tightly with the SHMR. The $W_{\rm MgII}$ peaks at the same characteristic mass as the SHMR, coinciding with a transition of the cool CGM from super-virial to sub-virial kinematics. Low-mass halos show excess non-gravitational motions consistent with recycled accretion and feedback-driven circulation, whereas massive halos show halo-centric heating that may maintain star formation quenching. This study bridges the gap between cool CGM and SHMR, showing that peak star formation efficiency coincides with the most abundant cool CGM reservoirs.

papers.title: Challenging the hoop conjecture with spinning pancakes and baguettes
papers.abstract: Understanding when gravitational collapse produces a black hole remains a central challenge in general relativity. Black-hole uniqueness results characterize the stationary endpoint under suitable assumptions, while singularity theorems establish geodesic incompleteness in the presence of trapped surfaces and appropriate energy and global conditions. Neither, however, provides a general criterion for horizon formation. The hoop conjecture offers such a criterion by relating the enclosed mass to the compactness of a matter distribution in every direction. We construct axisymmetric families of initial data describing rotating dust and test a formulation of the conjecture adapted to this setting. We explore highly prolate and oblate configurations with both constant and differential rescaled angular-velocity profiles, including configurations near the threshold for apparent-horizon formation. We find that the conjecture holds for rotating configurations, with a coefficient within 14% of unity as in the nonrotating case, provided the quasilocal mass includes the rotational energy. If the irreducible mass of the apparent horizon is used instead, the deviations grow with spin, as they do for Kerr black holes. For horizonless configurations, the conjecture likewise holds when the mass is restricted to the energy enclosed by the matter surface, whereas using the ADM mass, which also includes rotational field energy outside the matter, leads to apparent violations of up to $\approx$25%. We also discuss the possible evolution of compact configurations without apparent horizons, their relation to weak cosmic censorship, and their implications for horizonless compact objects.
papers.comments: 50 pages, 12 figures, 10 tables; v2: References added and discussion expanded

papers.title: A dual-moment phenomenological framework for gravitational,electromagnetic and strong interactions
papers.abstract: The unification of fundamental interactions remains an outstanding open problem in fundamental physics. Most existing unification schemes rely on extra dimensions, exotic symmetries, or unobserved dynamical degrees of freedom. Here we construct a minimal classical phenomenological framework built on primitive charges and motion-induced kinetic dual moments. Gravitational, electromagnetic, and strong interactions are coherently formulated within a unified inverse-square-law structure. We postulate a universal coupling relation connecting source-charge couplings and moment-mediated couplings across these interaction sectors. Although weak-charge degrees of freedom can be formally accommodated within the formalism, full quantitative treatment of weak-interaction dynamics is left for future work. The model recovers well-established low-energy limits for planetary orbits, atomic systems, and heavy-quark hadrons. Importantly, it yields distinguishable corrections to light deflection by rapidly spinning compact objects, and three independent experimental schemes are proposed to test these predictions.
papers.comments: 8 pages, 5 figures, Revised title and introduction for clarity. The numerical parameters for the flow experiment are updated to physically realizable values. The core theoretical framework remains unchanged

papers.title: Tracing Galactic Dust Reddening with Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Emission: SPHEREx Observations of the North Ecliptic Pole
papers.abstract: We investigate the ability of SPHEREx observations of the $3.3$ $\mu$m polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) emission feature to trace Galactic dust reddening. Applying a spectral template-based method to SPHEREx data, we measure the strength of the $3.3$ $\mu$m PAH feature in each $6''.2$ pixel of a $22^{\circ}$ by $22^{\circ}$ region centered on the north ecliptic pole (NEP). We convert the PAH feature strength to reddening by applying a radiation field correction and a linear scale factor. The resulting $E(B-V)$ map is consistent with far-infrared, stellar, and HI-based reddening maps at arcminute scales, exhibiting a typical $E(B-V)$ difference of $\lesssim 7$ mmag. A galaxy count test finds that all reddening maps have a dispersion of $\approx11$ mmag in $E(B-V)$ relative to what would be needed to produce spatially uniform galaxy counts. While there is some evidence that reddening is overestimated by our map at high PAH abundances, this effect is smaller than the uncertainties on the applied radiation field corrections and limited to $\sim$10 mmag in the most extreme regions of the NEP. For a diffuse, high Galactic latitude region like the NEP and at the sensitivities of our validation metrics, the SPHEREx PAH-emission based reddening map matches the accuracy of existing reddening maps while being capable of accessing a higher angular resolution of $\sim6''$.
papers.comments: 19 pages, 9 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to ApJ. Updated author list

papers.title: Exact transformation-optics representation of the Ellis wormhole and limits of finite-device scattering emulation
papers.abstract: We derive a global isotropic representation of the ultrastatic Ellis wormhole and establish which features of its electromagnetic response can, and cannot, be reproduced by a finite device. An orientation-preserving coordinate map sends the signed proper-radial line to a punctured Euclidean chart with refractive index $n(\rho)=1+a^2/(4\rho^2)$. Through the Plebański correspondence, this gives the exact impedance-matched continuum medium $\varepsilon_r=\mu_r=n(\rho)\mathbf{I}$ and its full vector-Maxwell operator. For the ideal two-ended geometry, we derive the electromagnetic radial operator, establish its spectral properties, and express its scattering amplitudes through Jost solutions and Wronskians. Nonzero transmission into the second asymptotic end implies $|R_{\rm id}|<1$ at every real frequency, whereas a regular, lossless finite one-port has unit-modulus reflection. The reverse triangle inequality therefore yields a strictly positive lower bound on the complex reflection-amplitude mismatch. This theorem applies to the stated lossless single-port class and is not extended to lossy or multiport realizations. We compute converged multipole scattering data and establish the low-frequency threshold scaling $|T_L|^2\propto(\omega a/c)^{4L+2}$, with coefficients independently validated for $L=1,2,3,4$. The transmission cross section tends to $\pi a^2$, while the ideal profile's total scattering cross section has a logarithmic forward divergence. We also construct a smooth finite-shell target and derive an exact finite-band constitutive-error formula for a calibrated passive Lorentz model. The constitutive benchmark is kept distinct from scattering equivalence throughout.
papers.comments: 14 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. v2: references to earlier work on wave scattering, grey-body factors and observational tests of wormholes added. Ancillary files contain the Python and MATLAB codes and the data needed to reproduce all figures and tables

papers.title: Simulation-Based Priors and BAO Shifts from the Lyman-$α$ Forest at the Field Level
papers.abstract: We present an analytic forward model for the Lyman-$\alpha$ (Ly-$\alpha$) forest flux field based on cubic-order large-scale structure perturbation theory (effective field theory) calculations. We validate our cubic model on two sets of hydrodynamic simulations spanning $2 \leq z \leq 4$: the small-volume CAMELS suite, which spans a wide range of cosmological and astrophysical parameters, and the large-volume, high-resolution Sherwood simulations. We find qualitatively similar results for both at the power-spectrum level. The perturbative model reproduces the three-dimensional flux power spectrum of the simulations to $\sim 5\%$ down to $k \simeq 1$-$1.5\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, depending on the redshift. This improves compared to previous quadratic perturbative forward models by up to 40%. Exploiting cosmic-variance cancellation in the field-level approach, we carry out precision measurements of the Lyman-alpha forest bias parameters from the CAMELS simulation suite. We use these measurements to analytically predict the shifts in the Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) scaling parameters induced by nonlinearities in the three-dimensional Lyman-alpha forest clustering as a function of cosmological parameters. We find sub-percent shifts in both the radial and transverse directions with a noticeable dependence on cosmology and redshift. Finally, from the field-level fits we construct simulation-based priors that can be used for cosmological analyses of the Lyman-alpha forest with the currently observing Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). In addition, our cubic model captures the connected four-point function (trispectrum) of the forest, which opens up novel opportunities for accurate covariance matrix estimation for DESI and its successor, DESI-II.
